### 465. Jer. 5:21-22

### 465. Jer. 5'21-22 (3_38) trans

Jonathan Edwards

D/3 March 1738

___________________________________________________________________

Jer 5. 21 . 22. Hear now this O Foolish People & without understanding which have eyes and see not which have ears & hear not, Fear ye not me saith the L. will ye not tremble at my Pres. which have placed the sand for the bound of the sea ------------------------------------------

_____________________________

The Prophet in this chap. declares the exceeding wicked ness of the People of Judah & Jerusalem & their boldness presumption & obstinacy in it against all warnings warning & shews how they disregarded Gods authority & made light of his threatnings G. in these words of the text is expostulating with them concerning their boldness & presumption in sin . & in the words may be Observed

__________________________

1. Wherein the People were criminal are Charged as being criminal viz in that they did not fear G. and tremble at his presence.

____________________

2. Their stupididity & selfishness of the People herein manifested . This Is is implied in the manner of the Charge vi its being by such in the way of such Earnest interrogationin Fear ye not me will ye not tremble at my P.The manner of expression[^012-note1] both implies that they did not fear G. & nor tremble ---------- and also implies that they terribly wicked & unreasonable & foolish in it as much as to say are ye so abun me have unreasonable as not to fear me are ye so monstrously stupid as not to tremble at the Pr. of such an one as I am .

__________________________

The occasion of what the Apostle in this Chap. writes to the Xtian Rom. seems to be certain differences & strifes that had risen Among them concerning some of the observances of the Ceremonial law particularly concerning those sorts of food that were forbidden und by that Ceremonial law & concerning those festival days that were therein appointed some of the Xtia there were many Jews that lived at Rome as appears by the last Chap. of the Acts of the Apostles & some of the Xtians that dwelt there that the Apostle sends this Epistle to had before been Jews and many of the Xtian Jews that were in those days in all parts of the Θ were very after their conversion to Xtianity were still very Zealous of the observances of the Ceremonial Law & urged the same upon the Gentile converts Hence arose a great difficulty in the Chh that was at Rome for held that it wa now under the Gospel Lawf. to eat those things that had been forbidden in the Law of Moses & another held it unlawfull one held it to be neces that the Jewish festivals were now abolished but Another held that it was necessary to observe em still Hence arose hot disputa. among them to the wounding of their Charity one towards another . Those [^013-note2] that held it to be necessary to Keep the Jewish festival days and to obstain from meats Ceremonially unclean were ready to condemn others that used their liberty & freely made use of Legally unclean meats & neglected the Jewish f did not observe the Jewish festivals & [ ] look upon them impious & doing transgressions of Gods Commands & on the other hand the others that were sensible that In these gospel days there was no obliga. lay upon Xtians to observe these things were ready to despise those that were Zealous of them for their weakness Ignorance & superstition & therefore the Apostle begins the Chapter . 1 2 3d vs & then the Apostle proceeds to speak of their observation of festival days 5 v 6 The Apostle Condemns their Censuring one another. & shews that there is room for charity on both sides notwithstanding such d a difference of opinion with Respect to thngs that were ceremonial & circumstantial. because tho both sides their opinions & practice in these things was different yet both sides might be conscientious truly conscientious in what they did. & might [^013-note3] act from a religious regard to Gods authority & Glory the one side was mistaken as to what w Gods commands were & theref the Apostle says v. 6. X was the same yesterday to day & forever. If They still Professed to be Xtians or the followers of J. X then they should still Cleave to the same doctrines that they were taught at their first Conversion they should still follow their f the faith of those that at had first taught them indoctrinated them in Xtianity . for J.
